title: Sebastian and the Spire
premise: Orsen Whitlock, a bone-carver who hears the voices of the dead lodged in the things they touched, has spent years quietly keeping the ledgers of the Gilderscale, a guild that trades in impossible objects. When the crown declares a hunt for 'the gifted,' Orsen's careful invisibility shatters: the dead begin screaming warnings, and Orsen learns the king himself died years ago, his body worn like a puppet by something bound inside the royal spire. Hunted by inquisitors and betrayed by the guildmaster who once sheltered them, Orsen must gather unlikely allies—a disgraced knight, a memory-thief, and the ghost of the true king—to climb the spire and unbind the crown before winter's long dark seals the city forever. In the end, Orsen chooses truth over loyalty to the guild that raised them, frees the king's spirit at terrible personal cost, and loses their own gift—only to discover that belonging was never something the dead could give them.
about_author: Beatrix Vane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing estate inventories and swears half of them whispered. She writes fantasy about people who keep records of things that should not exist.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Orsen Whitlock carves a bone button and hears its dead owner complain about the cold. POV: Orsen. Introduces the Gilderscale guild, its ledgers, and Orsen's gift as a quiet burden. Emotional beat: lonely competence—the comfort of routine hiding deep isolation.

chapters.title: What the Dead Keep
chapters.summary: A client brings a locket; the woman inside it begs Orsen to tell her daughter goodbye. Orsen refuses to get involved, as always. POV: Orsen. Establishes the rule: never answer the dead. Emotional beat: guilt dressed up as discipline.

chapters.title: The Guildmaster's Kindness
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Corvane Hale praises Orsen's discretion and hints at promotions—while quietly noting which clients ask about 'sensitive' items. POV: Orsen. We see Hale's warmth with an undertow of calculation. Emotional beat: gratitude laced with unease.

chapters.title: Proclamation at the Market Cross
chapters.summary: Heralds read the crown's decree: all gifted persons must register or be taken. The market goes silent. POV: Orsen. First public threat; neighbors' eyes turn suspicious. Emotional beat: the floor dropping out of an ordinary life.

chapters.title: Voices Rising
chapters.summary: That night every object in Orsen's workshop speaks at once—the dead sense the hunt too, and they are afraid. POV: Orsen. The gift becomes unbearable noise. Emotional beat: terror of being known by everything you touch.

chapters.title: The Knight Who Lost Her Name
chapters.summary: Disgraced knight Sera Voss arrives to sell her sword; the blade remembers every man she killed. She recognizes what Orsen is—and says nothing. POV: alternating Orsen/Sera. Two hunters-of-a-sort circle each other. Emotional beat: wary recognition between the hunted.

chapters.title: Registration Day
chapters.summary: Orsen forges ledger entries to hide three gifted clients, risking the guild itself. Hale watches, saying nothing. POV: Orsen. First act of open defiance. Emotional beat: the intoxicating fear of choosing a side.

chapters.title: The Thing in the King's Portrait
chapters.summary: Restoring a commissioned frame, Orsen hears a voice from a royal portrait—not the king's, but something older wearing his shape, humming a hunger-song. POV: Orsen. First hint the crown itself is wrong. Emotional beat: dread with a hook of terrible curiosity.

chapters.title: Sera's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sera returns, offering protection in exchange for Orsen reading her dead brother's ring—she needs to know if she betrayed him. POV: Sera. Her backstory surfaces: cashiered for refusing an order tied to the palace. Emotional beat: two debts offered across a table.

chapters.title: Inquisitor Marr
chapters.summary: Crown inquisitor Marr visits the Gilderscale, courteous and awful, testing ledgers against bone-dust readings. Orsen lies flawlessly and nearly dies of it. POV: Orsen. A worthy antagonist introduced. Emotional beat: the vertigo of lying to power.

chapters.title: The Memory-Thief
chapters.summary: Orsen seeks Wren Quill, a thief who steals memories from objects, to learn how to silence the voices. Wren names a price: one of Orsen's own memories, chosen blind. POV: Wren. New ally, new danger. Emotional beat: fascination shadowed by self-erasure.

chapters.title: What Orsen Forgot
chapters.summary: Wren takes a memory; Orsen feels a hole shaped like a person but can't say who. POV: Orsen. The cost lands. Emotional beat: grief without a name—thematic heart of the book.

chapters.title: Hale's True Ledger
chapters.summary: Orsen discovers a hidden second ledger: Hale has been selling gifted clients to the crown for years. POV: Orsen. The mentor revealed as betrayer. Emotional beat: betrayal that recontextualizes every kindness.

chapters.title: Flight from the Gilderscale
chapters.summary: Marr returns with warrants; Hale hands over names, including Orsen's. Sera extracts Orsen through the guild's bone-cellars as the workshop burns. POV: alternating. The old life ends in smoke. Emotional beat: loss and liberation tangled together.

chapters.title: The Undercity of Kept Things
chapters.summary: Sera leads Orsen to the Undercity, where smugglers warehouse cursed goods. The dead here are louder—and some are organizing. POV: Orsen. World expands; the dead have politics. Emotional beat: awe and claustrophobia.

chapters.title: The Ghost Who Was King
chapters.summary: A regal shade finds Orsen: Aldric, the true king, murdered seven years ago. He asks Orsen to hear his testimony. POV: Aldric (first ghost-POV). The conspiracy's scale revealed. Emotional beat: the weight of a kingdom's stolen grief.

chapters.title: Testimony of Bones
chapters.summary: Aldric leads Orsen to his hidden remains; touching them, Orsen experiences the murder from inside it—the spire, the binding, the thing called the Hollow Crown. POV: Orsen living another's death. Emotional beat: horror transformed into resolve.

chapters.title: Wren's Price Revisited
chapters.summary: Wren admits the memory they took from Orsen holds the name of someone Orsen loved—someone connected to the palace. They offer to return it. POV: Wren. Their own guilt over a stolen childhood surfaces. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness.

chapters.title: The Name in the Hole
chapters.summary: The memory returns: Orsen's sister Lys, taken by the crown's registry years ago—alive, serving in the spire. POV: Orsen. Personal stakes fuse with the plot. Emotional beat: hope sharp enough to cut.

chapters.title: Winter Begins
chapters.summary: The Hollow Crown accelerates its ritual; snow falls that doesn't melt, and the city's fires burn blue. Days shorten unnaturally. POV: multiple vignettes. The stakes become environmental and civic. Emotional beat: collective dread.

chapters.title: Recruiting the Undercity
chapters.summary: Orsen bargains with the smuggler-council: testimony against Hale and post-liberation trade rights in exchange for men, maps, and silence. POV: Orsen growing into leadership. Emotional beat: the surprising sweetness of being trusted.

chapters.title: Marr Closes In
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Marr traces Aldric's bones; a running battle through the Undercity costs lives. Sera is wounded holding the line. POV: Sera. Her redemption arc ignites. Emotional beat: fierce protectiveness hardening into love.

chapters.title: The Dead Vote
chapters.summary: The Undercity's ghosts convene—will they lend Orsen their strength? An old grudge against the living nearly sinks it until Aldric kneels to them. POV: Aldric. Political climax among the dead. Emotional beat: reconciliation across the grave-line.

chapters.title: Lys
chapters.summary: Orsen infiltrates the spire's lower offices and finds Lys—complicit, broken, believing the Crown protects her. She betrays Orsen's presence rather than leave. POV: Lys. The reunion curdles. Emotional beat: heartbreak of loving someone the system remade.

chapters.title: Captured
chapters.summary: Guards take Orsen to Marr, who offers registration, comfort, purpose—if Orsen will read the Hollow Crown's bindings and help strengthen them. POV: Orsen. Temptation framed as mercy. Emotional beat: the seduction of surrender.

chapters.title: The Cell of Quiet
chapters.summary: Imprisoned in a warded cell where no dead can speak, Orsen confronts total silence for the first time since childhood—and realizes how much of themselves was built on the voices. POV: Orsen. Dark night of the soul. Emotional beat: terrifying stillness, then clarity.

chapters.title: Sera and Wren Break the Spire's Back Door
chapters.summary: The allies assault the spire's undercrofts using Wren's stolen memories as keys. Sera faces her old commander and refuses to become him. POV: Sera/Wren. Action midpoint of the endgame. Emotional beat: courage as a choice made repeatedly.

chapters.title: Hale's Confession
chapters.summary: Captured Hale, broken by Marr's suspicion, reveals the binding ritual's structure—and that he sold Orsen's parents decades ago. POV: Hale. Villain given tragic dimension. Emotional beat: pity without forgiveness.

chapters.title: Escape Through the Walls
chapters.summary: The spire's stones remember everyone executed there; Orsen convinces the walls themselves to open. Ghosts pour into the corridors. POV: Orsen. The gift weaponized at last. Emotional beat: exhilaration of finally fighting as yourself.

chapters.title: Lys Chooses
chapters.summary: In the chaos, Orsen reaches Lys again—this time offering truth instead of rescue. She opens the inner gate and stays behind to hold it. POV: Lys. Redemption purchased at risk. Emotional beat: forgiveness as a door, not a debt.

chapters.title: The Ascent
chapters.summary: Orsen, Sera, Wren, and Aldric climb the spire through nine floors of binding-wrought horrors, each floor demanding a memory or a truth. POV: rotating. Gauntlet structure. Emotional beat: sacrifice as toll, paid willingly.

chapters.title: The Floor of Orsen's Mother
chapters.summary: One floor replays Orsen's mother's arrest; Orsen must watch without intervening to pass. The forgotten memory completes itself. POV: Orsen. Most intimate trial. Emotional beat: mourning finally allowed to finish.

chapters.title: The Hollow Crown
chapters.summary: At the summit: the king's body enthroned, the entity within—a famine-spirit bound by the founders—feeding on the city's warmth to survive winter. It offers Orsen a place among the kept things. POV: Orsen. Confrontation with the antagonist's logic. Emotional beat: temptation at the threshold.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: The ritual requires a witness who can hear both sides: Orsen reads the original binding aloud while Aldric testifies, unraveling the pact that traded a king for a harvest. POV: Aldric/Orsen duet. Climactic magic as courtroom and exorcism. Emotional beat: truth as the only blade that works.

chapters.title: The King Dies Twice
chapters.summary: Freed, Aldric's spirit must still leave his desiccated body—and the world. His farewell to Orsen is the book's emotional peak. POV: Aldric. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into gratitude; letting go as the final loyalty.

chapters.title: What the Famine Left
chapters.summary: The entity, unbound but starving, offers a last bargain: winter's end for one willing vessel. Sera steps forward; Orsen stops her—and Wren gives the famine their hoarded memories instead, emptying themselves. POV: Wren. Sacrifice with ambiguous cost. Emotional beat: love expressed as loss.

chapters.title: Thaw
chapters.summary: Snow melts; Marr, witnessing the entity's nature, burns the registry and walks away from the crown's service. The city wakes confused but alive. POV: multiple. Aftermath begins. Emotional beat: exhausted dawn.

chapters.title: Ledgers Closed
chapters.summary: Orsen returns to the ruined Gilderscale, formally closes the impossible-ledgers, and releases every bound object's dead. Hale awaits judgment by the survivors' council. POV: Orsen. Accountability without cruelty. Emotional beat: justice as housekeeping of the soul.

chapters.title: Quiet, At Last
chapters.summary: Orsen's gift has faded—most days. In the rebuilt shop, a single bone button whispers hello, and Orsen answers, gently. POV: Orsen. The theme resolves: connection chosen, not compelled. Emotional beat: peace earned, not granted.

chapters.title: Sebastian and the Spire
chapters.summary: Epilogue: spring. Orsen, Sera, and a hollowed-but-healing Wren plant a garden where the spire's shadow used to fall. A child asks why the tower was torn down; Orsen begins, 'There was a king...' POV: Orsen. Full-circle close. Emotional beat: belonging found in the telling of the story itself.
